questions.question: Describe a software-development task from your test-automation work that required you to interface with hardware or test equipment. How would you translate that experience into developing and debugging microprocessor firmware?

A PCB designer asks for guidance on routing a board containing a microcontroller, image sensor interface, power regulators, and fast digital lines. What placement and routing constraints would you provide, and why?
This team may use PAD PCB design tools. How would you learn the tool while ensuring that library choices, design rules, and manufacturing outputs are reliable?

How would you partition responsibilities between an FPGA and a microcontroller in a high-throughput image-capture system, particularly for timing-critical acquisition, buffering, configuration, and diagnostics?

This position requires onsite work five days per week and close interaction with manufacturing. What specifically motivates you to move from hardware test and repair into this hands-on digital engineering role, and how would you build effective day-to-day relationships with production partners?
What experience do you have with the NXP i.MX family or similar application processors? How would you structure early hardware and firmware bring-up for a board using one?
Have you used DX Designer for schematic capture or PCB design? If not, how would you transfer your schematic-reading and hardware-test knowledge into a DX Designer design-review workflow?
What microprocessor- or microcontroller-based hardware have you personally worked with, and what was your specific responsibility in its design, programming, bring-up, or test?

Walk me through how you would review a captured schematic for a new microcontroller-based image-capture board before it is released for layout. What checks would you make for power, reset, clocks, interfaces, and testability?

What experience, if any, do you have with Texas Instruments Code Composer Studio? If it is new to you, outline how you would bring up, build, flash, and debug a TI microcontroller project during your first week.
